0.title: VALERIUS FORMALLY REGISTERS HIS CIVIC CANDIDACY
0.news: Valerius completes the formal registration of his candidacy for the lowest-level civic election he announced at the close of the previous round. The registration is treated as a civic procedure rather than an assumption of office, and the officials record his candidacy without granting him powers that belong to the eventual officeholder. The remaining procedural steps are explained to him, including the period in which the local electorate may question candidates before voting. Valerius accepts the process on those terms and does not claim an electoral result that has not occurred. His declaration has therefore become an established candidacy, while the election itself remains unresolved.

1.title: THE SIXTH SURPLUS DELIVERY SETTLES
1.news: The next scheduled delivery under Valerius's recurring surplus agreement reaches settlement during the week. The completed consignment produces 33 denarii in gross receipts against 12 denarii in operating costs, leaving 21 denarii of realized net public profit. Under the standing account-routing rule, 2.1 denarii is transferred to Valerius's private account and 18.9 denarii remains in the public account. The settlement concerns only the delivery actually completed and creates no booked future receipt. The shared-water road remains the established route for the merchants, and the transaction continues the existing agreement rather than creating a new contract.

2.title: A SEPARATE LOCAL SURPLUS SALE CLEARS ANOTHER STORE
2.news: A separate local sale of estate agricultural surplus is completed outside the recurring caravan agreement. The transaction brings 17 denarii in gross receipts and incurs 7 denarii in operating costs, producing 10 denarii of realized net public profit. The established ten-percent routing sends 1 denarius to Valerius's private account while 9 denarii remains public. Because the sale is a distinct local transaction, it does not alter the terms or cadence of the recurring merchant agreement. The completed sale also leaves the estate's fixed agriculture metric unchanged because agriculture is already at its canonical cap.

3.title: VALERIUS ACQUIRES SIX ADDITIONAL ACRES ADJOINING THE ESTATE
3.news: Valerius completes the purchase of a six-acre strip adjoining his existing holdings. The acquisition costs 9 denarii from the public estate account and adds 0.009375 square miles to the canonical land total. Estate stewards mark the new boundary and begin recording it as part of the holding rather than treating the purchase as an unrecorded intention. No immediate increase is applied to the capped agriculture metric merely because the land has changed ownership. The acquisition is therefore realized as property and boundary expansion, with future use left to subsequent decisions and events.

4.title: A SECOND DISPLACED HOUSEHOLD IS ADMITTED UNDER VALERIUS'S PROTECTION
4.news: A second displaced household reaches the estate seeking the same protection that was extended to the earlier refugee family. Valerius accepts the household under his established protective policy, and the stewards record three additional residents within the estate community. The newcomers are given ordinary living arrangements and are not treated as a separate military or political body. Their admission raises the recorded population from 254 to 257 people. The guard establishment remains unchanged, with protection continuing through the existing 100-man personal guard rather than through a new recruitment levy.

5.title: THE FULL PERSONAL GUARD COMPLETES A READINESS EXERCISE
5.news: Titus Varenus oversees a full readiness exercise involving the established 100-man personal guard, with its 50 infantry and 50 cavalry personnel accounted for. The exercise tests assembly, movement, communication, and return to ordinary guard stations without removing any men from permanent availability. The formation completes the drill without injury or disciplinary disruption. Readiness and the other capped military metrics remain unchanged because they are already at their canonical maximums. The exercise nevertheless confirms that the existing guard establishment remains operationally coherent.

6.title: A WEATHERED STONE MARKER CHANGES THE ROAD INVESTIGATION
6.news: The continuing examination of the older secondary road alignment produces an unexpected physical clue when Publius Servilius and Numerius Cassius uncover a weathered stone marker partly buried beside the maintained route. The surviving mark is deliberate but incomplete, and the men cannot yet establish a builder, date, authority, or original purpose from the fragment alone. Cassius records the stone's position and condition while Servilius preserves the surrounding context instead of moving it or treating an uncertain reading as a conclusion. The finding gives Valerius a new object of investigation and expands the road inquiry beyond the alignment itself into the possibility that surviving markers may identify the administration or community responsible for the work. No final attribution is made in this round, and the investigation remains open.
